title: Time Needed to Buy Tickets
statement:
People stand in a single line at a ticket counter; person `i` (with person `0` at the front) wants `tickets[i]` tickets. Every second, whoever is at the front buys exactly one ticket. If they still want more, they rejoin the back of the line at once; if they now have all their tickets, they leave.

Return how many seconds pass until the person who started at index `k` has bought all of their tickets.
notes:
## Intuition

Moving people to the back of a real queue is unnecessary. Nobody ever overtakes anyone, so the line always cycles through the people in their original order, skipping those who already left. One pass over the array is therefore one "round" of the queue, and we can simulate it with a counter per person.

## Approach

1. Copy `tickets` into `remaining` and set `time = 0`.
2. Repeat rounds: sweep `i` from the front to the back of the array.
3. Skip anyone whose `remaining[i]` is already 0; they have left the line.
4. Otherwise that person buys one ticket: decrement `remaining[i]` and add one second to `time`.
5. As soon as person `k` reaches 0, return `time`.

## Example 1, step by step

`tickets = [2, 3, 2]`, `k = 2`. Round 1: each person buys one, `remaining` becomes `[1, 2, 1]` and `time = 3`. Round 2: person 0 buys (`time = 4`, done), person 1 buys (`time = 5`), person 2 buys their last ticket at `time = 6`, so the answer is `6`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n · tickets[k]): there are at most `tickets[k]` rounds of `n` steps (at most 10^4 here).
- Space: O(n) for the copy.

The simulation also reveals a one-pass formula: everyone up to `k` buys `min(tickets[i], tickets[k])` tickets and everyone after `k` buys `min(tickets[i], tickets[k] - 1)`, because `k` finishes before they get their last turn of that round.

## Pitfalls

- Stop the moment person `k` finishes, in the middle of a round; people behind `k` do not buy in that final round.
- Skipped people take no time; only an actual purchase adds a second.
- Work on a copy if the caller's array must stay unchanged.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `remaining` | tickets each person still wants |
| `time` | seconds elapsed, one per ticket sold |
| `i` | the person currently at the counter in this round |

narration.2: Work on a copy so the caller's array is left alone.
narration.3: No tickets sold yet, so no time has passed.
narration.5: Keep running rounds of the queue until person k is done.
narration.6: One sweep visits everyone in their original queue order.
narration.7: Someone with nothing left has already left the line.
narration.8: Skip them; they take no time.
narration.10: The person at the counter buys one ticket...
narration.12: Did person k just buy their last ticket?
narration.13: Then this is the moment they finish.
